Subject: Fincrest: prioritized feature commitment request — deterministic routing & export SLA

Team —

Quick context: Fincrest (Alex) is moving toward a firm procurement decision contingent on two things we don't currently guarantee by default: deterministic request routing (pinning + instance affinity for an activation window) and an extended audit/export window for telemetry (90 days raw token-level telemetry + periodic redacted exports for compliance). They have signaled they will move to a 3-year committed contract if we can commit to a gated delivery plan by Jan 10.

What I'm asking for: can Product/Eng evaluate whether we can: 1) deliver a deterministic routing policy (pinning per-tenant for a specified activation window with fallback rules) and 2) provide a scoped audit export flow (90-day raw telemetry export, redaction pipeline and S3 delivery contract) on an accelerated path? Fincrest needs: 200 QPS peak, 95th percentile latency <= 220ms, and a guaranteed export snapshot every 24h.

I've attached our mutual action plan draft (Fincrest_MutualActionPlan_v1.pdf) and pasted the customer's timelines below. If we can sketch a realistic delivery plan (MVP + canary + full rollout) and a tradeoff list by EOD Thursday I can lock in the customer's verbal commitment and start legal/procurement engagement.

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel

Subject: Re: Fincrest: prioritized feature commitment request — deterministic routing & export SLA

Monica — thanks for the heads up and the MAP. A few clarifying points before we spin up a formal plan:

- On "deterministic routing": do they require strict instance affinity (same GPU worker) or just logical routing guarantees (route-to-residency group / tenant cache affinity)? The implementation surface and risk profile are very different.
- QPS: is 200 sustained or burst? Also, what's the expected session length / tokens per minute?
- Export: raw token-level telemetry for 90 days is a storage and privacy risk; we need their list of exactly which telemetry fields are required. Redaction policy and PII handling will determine effort.

From an engineering POV we can propose a staged approach: (A) policy layer + route-key tagging (low effort), (B) residency affinity with cache warmup and pinning (medium effort, needs infra changes), (C) strict instance pinning + SLA (high effort, needs infra + scheduler work).

If Alex confirms that route-key + residency affinity satisfies them for the contract we could probably scope an MVP for Q1. If they need strict instance pinning with guaranteed worker-level cache, that's a larger project and needs a prioritization slot.

Can we get explicit answers to the three bullets above from the customer today? If not, I propose we draft two commitment tiers for legal: Tier 1 (route-key + 72h residency pin, daily redacted export) and Tier 2 (instance-level pinning + 90-day raw export + SLA) with different pricing.

—Ben
Ben Carter

ben@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fincrest: prioritized feature commitment request — deterministic routing & export SLA

Monica, Ben — appreciate the quick follow. To clarify: Fincrest's security/compliance team will accept residency affinity (route-key + guaranteed warm pool) for the first 6 months if we get a written commitment to ship instance-level pinning as an add-on within 9 months. In other words: short-term suffices if we commit to the roadmap item and sign-off milestones.

QPS: 200 peak sustained with spikes up to 350 for short periods. Typical session token usage is ~250 tokens per session, average 1.5 sessions/sec across the tenant during peak windows.

Export: We will require raw telemetry fields for prompt/response IDs, timestamps, trace IDs and model variant used. We understand redaction needs; our GC/Privacy team will accept an encrypted S3 export with access controls for audit teams.

Timeline: Procurement is ready to move if Product provides a plan and legal sees Tiered commitments in the contract draft by Jan 10. We're willing to sign an MOU contingent on that plan.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Platform & Integrations, Fincrest Health
alex@fincrest.com

On Sun, Dec 20, 2026 at 11:05 AM Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com> wrote:
> From an engineering POV we can propose a staged approach: (A) policy layer + route-key tagging (low effort), (B) residency affinity with cache warmup and pinning (medium effort, needs infra changes), (C) strict instance pinning + SLA (high effort, needs infra + scheduler work).

Summarizing technical constraints and a proposed delivery plan:

1) MVP (4 weeks): route-key tagging + policy enforcement + nightly redacted export (24h snapshot). This requires work on the router and export pipeline only. Low risk.
2) Phase 2 (8–12 weeks from greenlight): residency affinity with warm-pool seeding + tenant pin window (72h configurable). Medium risk: needs scheduler changes and cache lifecycle adjustments.
3) Phase 3 (longer lead, ~6–9 months): instance-level pinning (worker-level affinity), SLA instrumentation, expanded export with encrypted raw telemetry retention. High risk: scheduler, autoscaler, and infra changes; may require dedicated capacity offering or a formal Dedicated contract.

I've attached an impact matrix that maps effort vs risk vs customer promise. If Product (Marissa) can confirm that Q1 roadmap can absorb Phase 2 as a prioritized ticket, we can offer Tier 1 in the contract with a Phase 3 roadmap commitment. Otherwise, we'll need a paid Dedicated slot or to push pricing materially.
